title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
description: U.S. federal investigators have linked executives at ransomware negotiation firms to the ShinyHunters hacking group, which has extorted over $70 million in 2026. ShinyHunters recently breached the FBI recruitment website, stealing sensitive personnel data. Arrests include a Dutch hacker and a Canadian cybersecurity executive charged with extortion-related offenses. Evidence suggests some executives had advance knowledge of breaches and may have helped operate ShinyHunters' extortion website. The investigation also uncovered a murder-for-hire plot linked to the group. The ShinyHunters extortion site pressured victims to pay ransoms under threat of data publication.
aiSummary: The ShinyHunters hacking group, active since 2019 and responsible for numerous major data breaches, has been linked by U.S. federal investigators to executives at ransomware negotiation firms in the U.S. and Canada. These executives maintained close relations with ShinyHunters, with one U.S. executive allegedly assisting in operating the ShinyHunters extortion website 'shinywire.com', which pressured victims to pay ransoms by threatening data exposure. The group extorted over $70 million in 2026 and notably breached the FBI recruitment site, stealing sensitive employee data. Arrests include Pepijn van der Stap in the Netherlands and Edward Dubrovsky in Canada, the latter charged with extortion-related crimes. Communications intercepted from Van der Stap revealed frequent contact with ransomware negotiators and knowledge of breaches before victims were informed. The investigation also revealed a murder-for-hire plot linked to Van der Stap. The ShinyHunters extortion site listed nearly 100 victim organizations, urging ransom negotiations and threatening data publication if ignored.
aiImpact: ShinyHunters has caused significant financial extortion exceeding $70 million in 2026 alone. The group compromised sensitive data from numerous organizations, including the FBI, exposing personal and classified information. The involvement of ransomware negotiation executives suggests potential insider collusion, undermining trust in incident response processes. The breach of FBI personnel data poses risks to national security and individual privacy. The extortion website pressured victims into paying ransoms under threat of public data exposure, increasing operational and reputational risks for affected organizations. The investigation uncovered a murder-for-hire plot linked to the group, indicating potential physical security threats beyond cybercrime.
